newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean Jan-May o'seas investment approvals fall.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean Jan-May o'seas investment approvals fall.

text.p: Approvals given to South Korean companies for overseas investment totalled $2.23 billion for the first five months of this year, down from $2.73 billion a year earlier, the central Bank of Korea (BOK) said on Monday.
In May alone, approvals for overseas investment fell sharply to $365.5 million from $781.2 million in the same month of 1996, a BOK report said. It did not give background.
Overseas investment by South Korean companies implemented during the January-May period also fell to $1.57 billion from $2.18 billion in the same five-month period in 1996.
But actual investment made during May rose to $342.2 million from $280.5 million a year ago, the report said.
China was the preferred destination for South Korean investment, with approvals for investment in China totalling $404.7 million during the five-month period.
The amount was down from $777.7 million for the same period of 1996, the bank said.
Approvals for investment in the United States totalled $299.4 million during the five-month period, down from $642.4 million a year ago, it said.
